title: Playbook ranking and synthetic runbook generator for contextual triage
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: On-call responders frequently spend the first minutes of an incident figuring out what runbook or checklist applies. This PR implements a lightweight, context-aware playbook ranking service plus a synthetic runbook generator that can produce concise, executable checklists for low-confidence matches. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-action by surfacing the top 3 playbooks with per-step confidence and a short, runnable fallback when no high-confidence playbook exists. Key design points: 1) A ranking model that scores playbooks by signal blend (alert fingerprinting, recent cluster-level events, recent triage comments, affected services). 2) A synthetic-runbook generator that emits a minimal checklist using existing templates and a constrained language model with deterministic scaffolding. 3) Opt-in rollout flagged by a config gate and telemetry to validate utility before enabling on-call autopopulation. Backwards compatibility: the default behavior preserves existing runbook selection flows unless the feature flag is enabled. Checklist: - [x] Implement playbook ranker service and API - [x] Add synthetic runbook generator with deterministic template mapping - [x] Hook ranking output into incident slack/cards UI as an opt-in toggle - [x] Add unit and integration tests that run on CI - [x] Add telemetry: selection_rate, acceptance_rate, median_time_to_first_action - [x] Provide documentation and admin toggle in Console Rollout plan: start behind the feature flag for 10% of incidents by volume for 2 weeks, collect metrics and qualitative feedback, then scale to 50% / 100% after sign-off. Safety and audit: generated runbooks include a provenance header and a checksum; generation is logged to the incident audit trail. Related work: Linear ENG-4921 (playbook discovery), ENG-4999 (oncall UX experiment).
commits: feat(ranker): new playbook ranker service with basic scoring pipeline
feat(generator): synthetic runbook generator and deterministic template resolver
chore(ci): add integration job for playbook-ranking smoke tests
test: unit tests for ranker and generator, add fixture incidents
docs: playbooks.md additions and admin toggle docs
changes_summary: Adds an opt-in ranking service that scores candidate playbooks and a synthetic-runbook generator for fallback. Integrates ranked candidates into Slack/card UI and adds telemetry hooks. Includes unit/integration tests and docs. Keeps existing behavior behind a feature flag.
review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice work. Two quick asks: add a test for the case where multiple playbooks have identical scores, and make the feature flag expire after 90 days if not promoted.
Maya Patel: Added deterministic tie-breaker in ranker (timestamp + id) and included a flag expiry policy in the admin docs.
Renee Ortiz: Can we ensure the generated runbook never includes destructive commands without a human confirmation step?
Maya Patel: Generator now tags steps with 'requires_confirmation' when a step matches destructive patterns; the UI renders a confirmation prompt. Added unit tests.
Diego Morales: CI flaked on the first integration run; reran and green now. Looks good to me. Approving.
release_notes: Add an opt-in contextual playbook ranking and synthetic-runbook generator to reduce time-to-first-action for on-call responders. Disabled by default behind a feature flag. Telemetry and admin controls included.
notes_for_ops: Feature is disabled by default. To enable: set incident.playbook_ranking.enabled=true in the admin Console and configure rollout percentage. Monitor metrics: incident.playbook.selection_rate, incident.playbook.acceptance_rate, incident.time_to_first_action.
testing_instructions: Run unit tests: pytest tests/test_playbook_ranker.py tests/test_synth_generator.py. For integration: run ci/pipeline.yml job 'integration-smoke' or run locally with the provided fixture incidents. Enable the feature flag in staging to exercise the Slack card UI.
observability_changes: Adds metrics: incident.playbook.ranked_count, incident.playbook.selection_rate, incident.playbook.acceptance_rate, incident.playbook.generator_confidence_histogram. Adds tracing spans for runbook.ranker.score and runbook.generator.generate.
security_considerations: Generator output includes provenance and checksum; a sanitation pass disallows inline secrets and strips raw keys. Steps matching destructive patterns are marked to require explicit human confirmation.
user_impact: Opt-in; when enabled users will see ranked playbooks in the incident view and a short generated checklist if no high-confidence playbook is found. Expected positive impact: faster triage and fewer handoffs.
qa_signoff: Renee Ortiz: signed off 2026-02-20 after validation in staging.
support_notes: If customers report unexpected runbook content, disable incident.playbook_ranking.generator.enabled and collect the incident ID and generator logs (runbook.generator.trace_id) for debugging.
